title: River Development Agent Production Execution-Package Creation Lifecycle Integration
objective: Establish the production integration boundary that consumes existing proposal, implementation-manifest, and execution-verification artifacts through the existing repository-safe artifact-loading contract and delegates those loaded artifacts to the authoritative execution-package creator without reconstructing upstream artifacts, duplicating package creation, executing implementation operations, or manufacturing execution authority.

architecture.authoritativeCreationBoundary: createExecutionPackage remains the sole authoritative execution-package construction boundary.
architecture.execution: DEV-330 does not directly invoke the implementation runner or execute package operations.
architecture.downstreamLifecycle: A successfully created execution package must remain compatible with the existing persistence lifecycle and the DEV-329 governed persisted-package execution path.
architecture.snapshotSemantics: The existing createExecutionPackage boundary intentionally structuredClone snapshots proposal, manifest, and verification into the execution package. DEV-330 must preserve source provenance and semantic content across that boundary and must not impose reference-identity requirements that contradict the authoritative creator.
architecture.executionAuthority: DEV-330 creates no operation-execution authorization, broadens no authorization, consumes no authorization, and does not treat apply mode as authorization.
architecture.existingProductionCommand: createExecutionPackageRiverDev is the already-established authoritative repository-path loading and package-creation command boundary. DEV-330 contract-hardens and proves this existing boundary through command-level integration coverage; no production-command mutation is required absent a demonstrated behavior gap.
architecture.defaultDeny: Missing, inaccessible, malformed, inconsistent, unapproved, unverified, or otherwise invalid source artifacts must continue to fail closed through existing policy and execution-package validation boundaries.
authoritativeInputs: Existing RiverDevImplementationProposal artifact loaded from its repository path.
Existing RiverDevImplementationManifest artifact loaded from its repository path.
Existing RiverDevExecutionVerificationMetadata artifact loaded from its repository path.

invariants: Do not create a second proposal representation or producer.
Do not create a second implementation-manifest representation, loader, or producer.
Do not create a second execution-verification representation or manufacture verification state.
Do not reconstruct proposal, manifest, or verification content merely to satisfy the integration boundary.
Do not bypass createExecutionPackage when constructing an execution package.
Do not directly invoke executePackage, the implementation runner, or repository mutation operations from the DEV-330 creation integration.
Do not manufacture, acquire, synthesize, upgrade, or broaden operation-execution authorization.
Do not infer authorization from requested apply mode.
Do not weaken existing plan ID, branch, proposal approval, verification, operation, readiness, or package validation invariants.
Preserve repository-path safety for all artifact inputs.
Preserve deterministic package creation for equivalent valid source artifacts.
acceptanceCriteria: Production integration consumes proposal, manifest, and verification from their existing repository artifact paths.
Repository path validation remains authoritative for all three source artifact paths.
Loaded proposal, manifest, and verification are supplied to the existing createExecutionPackage boundary without an alternate package-construction implementation.
The resulting package retains semantic content and provenance from the loaded source artifacts while respecting createExecutionPackage structuredClone snapshot semantics.
Invalid or inconsistent proposal/manifest/verification inputs remain rejected by existing validation rather than repaired or normalized by DEV-330.
Successful creation performs no implementation writes.
Successful creation creates or broadens no execution authorization.
The resulting execution package remains compatible with the existing immutable persistence lifecycle.
A persisted resulting package remains compatible with the DEV-329 governed execute-package lifecycle.

Tests cover valid creation, repository-path rejection, malformed or invalid lifecycle inputs where applicable, proposal/manifest consistency enforcement, verification readiness enforcement, structuredClone snapshot behavior where relevant, absence of implementation writes, and deterministic results.
